approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs by crossover and mutation from scored survivors and fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process to accepted feedback from the current session. It samples functions over each fresh offspring field and buys successive maxima. After several batches without improvement, it limits eligibility to the forty highest predictive means. In those restricted batches the Parent already samples independent residuals with the original jittered marginal variances; elsewhere it retains correlated residuals. Predictive means still both define the eligible set and favor particular members within it.
approach.novelty: Remove only the fine predictive-mean preference within the restricted set by giving every eligible candidate the current archive mean as its allocation location. The original means still determine eligibility, and the independent residuals remain unchanged. The earlier location-removal experiment retained correlation; this tests the same location consumer under the independent-residual Parent, whose same-Parent sibling list is empty. It answers whether that retained guidance still contributes under the changed covariance condition, with a preregistered prediction of lower useful gain rather than a claim of performance improvement.

observed_bottleneck: The actual code Parent n-5e03d3ccd1b7 still fails to convert its broader independent-residual purchases into the formal Anchor endpoint level: complete Search mean 0.598677634482057 (seed SD 0.032920934204526436), paired change -0.008352681729073996 against n-cf8d309c06de. Its full incumbent-gain mass is 5.852782851596213 despite 271 improvements, and late mass is 1.0207513071470453. The limiting behavior is conversion to substantial useful gains, not lack of valid purchases or absence of residual exploration. Whether retained fine predictive-location preference helps under this new covariance condition is untested. n-8e00e5e9fc34 established a -0.023092425745076712 location-removal contrast only with correlated restricted residuals, so its sign cannot be transferred or subtracted from the Parent correlation contrast. Independent read-only reconstruction from all fifteen Parent Search logs and trajectories reproduces 72 restricted announcements, 720 restricted choices, 363 changed same-availability choices, 72 changed purchase sets and 320 displaced identities under the proposed constant-location replay, with exposure in 13 cells, zero paid-identity/mask/winner mismatches and both never-restricted cells retained. Evidence: nodes/n-5e03d3ccd1b7/analysis.json; nodes/n-8e00e5e9fc34/analysis.json; the Parent seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 summary.json and run.log files; policy/scratch/r0058-03-improve-L01/natural-exposure-summary.json and its fifteen explicitly indexed audit files, each citing its exact source log and trajectory. These replays have no unpurchased outcomes.

At a successful FingerprintPosterior.select call let mu be the original fitted raw-score mean vector, a=self.score_mean from the current accepted archive, s=self.score_scale, L the unchanged full posterior Cholesky factor including its actual successful jitter, and Z the one inherited normal array. Original mu still defines exact eligibility sorted by (-mu_i,i), and each position still chooses the first maximum in ascending available pool index, then removes only that identity. When unrestricted, use the original mu+s*(Z@L.T) without replacement. The independent residual law and marginal variances s**2*sum_j L_ij**2 stay exact; the fitted covariance is not diagonalized or refit. Prediction: eliminating candidate-dependent location decreases aggregate original-mean preference in active restricted selections versus a passive original-location replay on the same state, changes paid identities, and may reduce full/late useful gain and matched endpoint mean. finding_summary.headline: Fine predictive means remain useful with independent residuals: removal lowered selection preference, gains and mean score
finding_summary.insights: Fine mean preference still contributes after restricted residual correlation has been removed. This closes that conditional sign question at the registered descriptive scale; it does not establish a uniform task effect, an interaction obtained by subtracting sibling effects, or generalization beyond this Search panel. The Child remained 0.021461 below the formal Anchor. Full selected-stream GP mean-squared error changed only from 0.011217 to 0.011281, while removing its location preference lowered endpoint performance. That separates a useful predictive consumer from the question of how to improve the overall search. The molecular evidence shows continued elaboration of related ring-rich families: average largest generic-scaffold share rose from 28.6% to 29.5% overall and from 40.3% to 43.2% late. At the same time, within-batch similarity after excluding tiny fragments fell from 0.4121 to 0.4041. More local variation therefore coexisted with less useful progress, rather than establishing a cure for the conversion bottleneck. Unusual heteroatom halogenation and absent stereochemical assignments remain proposal limitations, not demonstrated causes of the score loss. A proposal/search scheme that preserves distinct coherent core and functional-group alternatives, or a ranking model aimed at substantial incumbent gains, is the kind of method change that could address the observed limitation; neither is tested here. Original GP errors beat the archive constant on the actually bought restricted molecules, but these paid-stream associations cannot score the unpurchased replay or prove mediation. The posterior approach remains open. Diagnostic time is nested in other timing, and no independent replication or trusted comparative task-safety conclusion is available.
finding_summary.results: The registered behavior occurred in 100 of 435 announcements. Within those restricted sets, 569 of 1,000 choices differed from the original-location replay; 98 purchase sets changed and 436 identities were displaced. Original predictive-mean sum fell from 437.246705 to 402.657100, while mean-rank sum worsened from 11,754 to 21,570. Eligibility, residuals, normal draws and the unrestricted rule passed the same-state checks. All 4,350 optimizer purchases joined to feedback; 323 of the 569 changed choices survived their batch and 96 later generated paid children, with 22 censored by the final batch. Full incumbent-gain mass fell from 5.852783 to 5.656162, and late gain from 1.020751 to 0.812268 over 2,175 purchases. Positive generating-parent gain also fell, although the signed generating-parent total became less negative. The complete mean score fell from 0.598678 to 0.585570, a paired change of -0.013108, exceeding the registered 0.002 loss criterion. Seed macro changes were -0.005059, -0.005032 and -0.029234; nine task/seed endpoints fell, three rose and three tied. Both never-restricted cells reproduced their Parent trajectories. There was no execution failure, and the primary isolation, activation and useful-gain falsifiers did not trigger.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic, amine and carbonyl families persist, with unusual heteroatom halogenation and undefined stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: n-c6895a38b8fd produces recognizable aromatic amides, aryl-linked cyclic amines and aza-aromatic/carbonyl frameworks, together with densely fused or enlarged rings and unusual heteroatom decorations. This assessment uses only frozen Search seeds 0/1/2. context.comparison says Child evaluation and matching to the actual code Parent n-5e03d3ccd1b7 are both complete, with no profile-mismatched seeds; all 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectories exist and were read, and no task comparison is missing. Each cell contains 300 accepted evaluations including ten initial observations; molecular counts below use the 290 accepted optimizer observations, totaling 4350 per node. They do not describe rejected proposals or the unpurchased candidate fields. Child paid molecules have median 28 heavy atoms, range 1–96; 4250/4350 have rings and 4197/4350 have an RDKit aromatic ring. Digest ring-closure rates 0.9713–0.9839 and aromatic-text presence rates 0.9701–0.9724 support the ring-rich reading; these are molecule-level text indicators, not fractions of atoms. The Child/Parent <=5-heavy-atom tails are 94/103 and >50-heavy-atom tails 51/43. N–halogen-bearing counts are 1006/834 and O–halogen-bearing counts 236/340, with overlap allowed. These are explicit bond-pattern flags, not measured instability. Potential tetrahedral-centre-bearing counts are 2537/2660 using RDKit FindMolChiralCenters with useLegacyImplementation=False; neither node assigns tetrahedral configuration, and both record zero formal charge. Neutral SMILES notation does not establish physiological neutrality. Pooled nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are Child 1767/1027 and Parent 1764/1037, with 100/107 empty scaffolds. The largest nonempty typed scaffold occurs in 283/4350 Child versus 158/4350 Parent molecules; generic counts are 499/4350 versus 362/4350. Thus many connectivity variants coexist with repeated local series; uniqueness is not evidence of synthetic feasibility. The audit retains full and late chemistry, both size tails, typed/generic scaffold counts and within-batch similarity including and excluding <=5-heavy-atom molecules for every paired cell. Late means optimizer ordinals 146–290, trajectory evaluations 156–300. Similarity uses radius-2 2048-bit Morgan Tanimoto and should not be mixed with historical sparse-count-fingerprint summaries. Drug-likeness is moderate structural resemblance only: no synthesis, stability, pKa, exposure or biological activity was measured. No exact absent target scaffold can be recovered from scalar scores alone. All gaps are conditional observations of these adaptive accepted Search streams, without claims about mechanism activation, mediation, generalization or score improvement. Evidence: policy/requests/r0058-03-improve-L01-molecular-assess-510ae642b909af11.json; policy/scratch/r0058-03-improve-L01-molecular/audit-manifest.json; policy/scratch/r0058-03-improve-L01-molecular/source-receipt.json. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
